content.value_statement: Protected binaries often stop analysis with anti-debugging, packing, and obfuscation checks. This skill organizes authorized investigation steps, evidence collection, and defensive recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Explains common Windows and Linux anti-debugging checks.
Summarizes anti-VM, packing, obfuscation, and virtualization concepts.
Outlines authorized analysis workflows for protected binaries.
Lists common tools used in malware analysis and reverse engineering.
Connects technical findings to defensive recommendations.
limitations: Requires explicit authorization and a defined analysis scope.
Does not replace legal review or organization-specific policy checks.
Provides guidance, not automated binary analysis or tool execution.
Examples must be adapted and validated in a controlled lab.

use_cases.title: Triage Protected Malware Samples
use_cases.description: Identify likely anti-analysis checks and plan a controlled investigation path.

use_cases.title: Review Product Protection Risks
use_cases.description: Understand how commercial protections may affect internal security testing.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reverse Engineering Exercises
use_cases.description: Teach anti-debugging and obfuscation concepts within approved training labs.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Protections
prompt_templates.prompt: I have written authorization to analyze this binary. These are my observations: [observations]. Identify likely anti-reversing mechanisms and safe next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Explain One Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused explanation of a detected technique.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how this anti-debugging check works in an authorized analysis context: [check]. Include evidence to collect and defensive notes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Malware Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized malware analysis plan for a sample that detects debuggers and virtual machines. Include scope limits and documentation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Bypass Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare safe analysis options for a protected binary with packing, anti-debugging, and string obfuscation. Prioritize reversible methods and evidence preservation.

output_examples.input: A sample exits when a debugger attaches and behaves differently in a virtual machine.
output_examples.output: Likely checks include anti-debugging and anti-VM detection. The response would propose controlled observation, evidence collection, and defensive reporting.

output_examples.input: A packed binary reaches a new execution point after startup in an approved lab.
output_examples.output: The skill would explain unpacking concepts, help document the transition point, and recommend preserving original and analyzed artifacts.

output_examples.input: A team needs training material about obfuscation in malware samples.
output_examples.output: The skill would organize topics such as control flow flattening, string encryption, and API hiding into an authorized lesson plan.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization before discussing bypass or unpacking steps.
Work in an isolated lab and preserve original artifacts.
Record evidence, assumptions, and defensive recommendations for each finding.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to bypass software licensing or access controls.
Applying examples on production systems without written approval.
Sharing bypass details without verifying the recipient and purpose.

faq.question: Is this skill for offensive use?
faq.answer: It is dual-use security content. Use it only for authorized analysis, malware defense, training, or research.

faq.question: Does the skill execute analysis tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but it does not run debuggers, unpackers, or scripts.

faq.question: Can it help with malware analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help analysts recognize anti-debugging, anti-VM, packing, and obfuscation behaviors.

faq.question: What authorization is required?
faq.answer: You need explicit written permission, a defined scope, and compliance with applicable laws and policies.

faq.question: Does it provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. Consult qualified legal or policy experts before work that may involve circumvention rules.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
